# The UpstreamDrift Platform {#sec-platform}

This chapter summarizes the platform capabilities the modeling pathway
builds on; the complete hot-linked inventory, including known gaps, is
in @sec-appendix-inventory.

| Model | Location | Notes |
|---|---|---|

## The counterfactual and energetics stack

The normative contract lives in the engine-core dynamics interface
([`_dynamics_interface.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/engine_core/_dynamics_interface.py)):
`compute_drift_acceleration`, `compute_control_acceleration`,
`compute_ztcf`, `compute_zvcf`, with the superposition identity
(@eq-superposition) stated as a contract. Engine implementations exist
for MuJoCo, Drake, Pinocchio, OpenSim, MyoSuite, the analytic pendulum
engines, and the Simscape bridge
([`engine_capabilities.md`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/docs/engines/engine_capabilities.md)).
On top of these sit the pointwise engine-agnostic evaluator with HDF5
persistence
([`ztcf_zvcf.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/simulation_backends/ztcf_zvcf.py)),
a MuJoCo delta-based counterfactual analyzer
([`counterfactuals.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/engines/physics_engines/mujoco/python/mujoco_humanoid_golf/counterfactuals.py)),
induced-acceleration analyzers, MuJoCo inter-segment power flow
([`power_flow.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/engines/physics_engines/mujoco/python/mujoco_humanoid_golf/power_flow.py)),
engine-agnostic work/power/impulse metrics
([`power_work_metrics.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/analysis/power_work_metrics.py)),
kinematic-sequence and coordination analytics
([`kinematic_sequence.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/biomechanics/kinematic_sequence.py),
[`coordination_metrics.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/src/shared/python/analysis/coordination_metrics.py)),
and the MATLAB BASE/ZTCF/DELTA/ZVCF pipeline of @sec-ztcf-variants.

## Why this platform is the right instrument

Three properties make UpstreamDrift suited to the timing question.
First, **one model, many engines**: the same `GolfModelParams`
specification renders to an analytic CPU reference backend and to
MuJoCo-family backends, so results can be cross-validated between
independent dynamics implementations (@sec-appendix-validation).
Second, **counterfactuals as first-class citizens**: the drift/control
split is a tested contract, not an ad-hoc analysis, so the S2
hypothesis of @sec-hypothesis can be evaluated with the same code on
every engine. Third, **reproducibility discipline**: the experiments in
@sec-methods are committed modules with recorded provenance, run by two
commands (@sec-appendix-repro), and their outputs are the only source of
every number in @sec-results.
